<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par85 />{{GHGmargin-letter|85|r}}
With a long vowel in the second syllable: (''d'') ''tĭqṭâl'', as {{GHGheb|text=תְּהוֹם|translate=the ocean, the deep}} (for ''tĭhâm''; in Assyrian the fem. ''tiâmtu'', constr. st. ''tiâmat'', is the usual word for ''sea''), unless it is to be derived with Delitzsch, ''Prolegomena'', p. 113, from the stem {{GHGheb|text=תהם}}; (''e'') ''tâqṭîl'' (in Arabic the usual form of the infinitive of conjugation II. which corresponds to the Hebrew {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}), e.g. from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=תַּכְלִית|translate=completeness}}; {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְבִּית|translate=increase, usury}}, with a parallel form {{GHGheb|text=מַרְבִּית}}; in a passive sense, {{GHGheb|text=תַּלְמִיד|translate=a disciple}}; (''f'') {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְטוּל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּפּוּחַ|translate=an apple}} (for ''tănpû<sup>a</sup>ḥ''); very frequently used to form abstracts, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּגְמוּל|translate=a benefit}} (also {{GHGheb|text=גְּמוּל}}); from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוּסָה|translate=a treading down}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּנוּפָה|translate=a waving}} (like {{GHGheb|text=תְּרוּמָה|translate=a lifting up}}, from the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} stem), {{GHGheb|text=תְּשׁוּקָה|translate=a longing}}, &c.; very frequently also as an abstract plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּהְפֻּכוֹת|translate=perverseness}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְבֻּלוֹת|translate=guidance}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּמְרוּרִים|translate=bitterness}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּנְחוּמִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=תַּנְחוּמוֹת|translate=consolation}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֻנִים|translate=toil}}.

{{center|XI. ''Nouns with Afformatives.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|s}}
52. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ל}} affixed. Perhaps {{GHGheb|text=חַשְׁמַל|translate=amber}}(?), and probably {{GHGheb|text=בַּרְזֶל|translate=iron}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּרְמֶל|translate=garden-land}} ({{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in both cases is probably a modification of the original ''ă'' in the tone-syllable), {{GHGheb|text=גִּבְעֹל|translate=bloom}}, cf. {{GHGpar|30|q}}.—According to Prätorius, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1903, p. 530 ff., ''al'' is an affix of endearment in the proper names {{GHGheb|text=מִיכַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמוּטַל}} (''little lizard''?) {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִיגַל}} (also {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִיגַ֫יִל}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|t}}
53. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ם}} affixed. With an original ''ăm'' as afformative, {{GHGheb|text=אוּלָם|translate=vestibule}} (although the ''ā'' in the ''sing''. remains unchangeable), plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֻֽלַמִּים}}; but in {{GHGheb|text=כִּנָּם|translate=a swarm of gnats}}, the {{GHGheb|text=ם}} is radical. With original afformative ''ŭm'', {{GHGheb|text=עֵירֹם}} (also {{GHGheb|text=עֵרֹם}}) ''naked'' (from {{GHGheb|text=עור}}), plur. {{GHGheb|text=עֵיֽרֻמִּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=7}}, parallel form {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹם}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עֲרוּמִּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=25}}.—To this class also belong the adverbs in ''ām'' and ''ōm'', mentioned in {{GHGpar|100|g}}, and many proper names, as {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשֹׁם}}, also {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשׁוֹם}}, and {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשׁוֹן}} (''patronymic'' {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשֻׁנִּי}}), {{GHGheb|text=מִלְכֹּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַמְרָם}}, &c.; but for {{GHGheb|text=פִּדְיוֹם|translate=ransom}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=49}}, probably {{GHGheb|text=פְּדוּיִם}} is to be read.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|u}}
54. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ן}} affixed. The {{GHGheb|text=ן}} is added by means of a simple helping vowel in {{GHGheb|text=כְּנַ֫עֵן|translate=Canaan}}, and {{GHGheb|text=צִפֹּ֫רֶן|translate=a finger nail}}; more frequently the addition is made by means of a tone-bearing ''ă'', which in Hebrew is modified to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} (as {{GHGheb|text=גַּרְזֶן|translate=axe}}) or lengthened to ''ā'' (but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֹֽרַנִּית}} and {{GHGheb|text=קְדֹֽרַנִּית}}); e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קִנְיָן|translate=a possession}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁלְחָן|translate=a table}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָרְבָּן|translate=an offering}}. From an original ''â'' being changed into an obscure ''ô'' we may probably explain such forms as {{GHGheb|text=דְּאָבוֹן|translate=a pining away}}; {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽרְבוֹן}} (also {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽרְבָן}}) ''a goad''; {{GHGheb|text=רְעָבוֹן|translate=hunger}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּאוֹן|translate=pride}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָמוֹן|translate=noise}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָזוֹן|translate=a vision}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁרְיוֹן|translate=a coat of mail}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַשָּׁאוֹן|translate=guile}} (the only instance with both {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} preformative and ''ôn'' afformative)<ref>The plurals {{GHGheb|text=נִצָּנִים|translate=flowers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=12}}, and {{GHGheb|text=קִמְּשֹׂנִים|translate=thorns}} appear to be formed directly from the singulars {{GHGheb|text=נֵץ}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נִצָה}}) and {{GHGheb|text=קִמּוֹשׂ}} with the insertion of ''ân'' (which in {{GHGheb|text=קמ׳}} is obscured to ''ôn''). See Nöldeke, Mand. Gr., p. 169, Rem. 3; similarly, according to Hoffmann, ‘Einige phöniz. Inschriften,’ p. 15 ({{GHGcite|title=Abh. der Gött. Ges. der Wiss.}}, xxxvi), {{GHGheb|text=עִזְּבוֹנִים|translate=wares}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=27|verse=14.16}} from {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫זֶב}}={{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫צֶן}}.</ref>; very frequently from the simple stem with an unorganic sharpening of the second radical, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זִכָּרוֹן|translate=memorial}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּלָּיוֹן|translate=destruction}} (''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=זִכְרוֹן}} and {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְיוֹן}}), &c.; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽרָיוֹן|translate=pregnancy}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הִרָּ׳}}) and {{GHGpar|93|uu}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִֽיקָלוֹן|translate=shame}}, for {{GHGheb|text=קִלְקָלוֹן}}. Proper names occur with the termination ''ûn'', as {{GHGheb|text=יְשֻׁרוּן}}, {{GHGpar|86|g}}, and others.
